messages:
alex: @channel p99 spike in prod streaming (us-west-2) started ~14:03 UTC, concurrent tail stalls, SLO breach p99=1.8s (goal 0.5s). Seeing router LB misrouting to a few overloaded shards. Metrics: link to dashboard https://dash.redwood/streams/overview?alert=4123456789

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident alert created: INC-4123456789. Paging oncall now. Runbook: streaming-tail-latency -> router/ingress -> check shard heatmap.

maria: I'm oncall. grabbing logs and heatmap. alex can you post the query you used for the heatmap?

alex: heatmap query (grafana):
```
sum by (shard) (rate(router_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="+Inf"}[5m]))
```
look for skewed p99 across shards, then map to LB weights.

jessica: looks like 3 shards (s-17,s-18,s-19) have p99 >> 3s, others ~200ms. ingress shows repeated reroutes from local zone -> eu-west fallback. possible policy bug in prefer-local failover.

priya: any customer impact? which customers hit the streaming stalls? need to notify CS if user-facing.

daniel: customer logs show a few high-throughput customers in us-west-2 experiencing increased retry rates and stream resets. IDs: cust-824, cust-991. Telemetry shows request fanout to overloaded shards due to routing table entries that were stale after a recent scaling event.

maria: ok mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable prefer-local for affected routes 2) drain overloaded shards 3) reroute weight to cold pool. Does that sound safe? :thinking_face: 

alex: yes. quick commands:
```
# set routing policy to global-fallback for route prefix /stream
redwoodctl route update --prefix /stream --policy global-fallback --dry-run=false

# reduce weight on shards s-17..19
redwoodctl shards set-weight s-17 s-18 s-19 --weight 0.1
```

jessica: executed route update -> global-fallback, confirmed via router config roll. weight reductions in flight.

incident-bot: Live action recorded: route update + weight changes. Automations: start tail log capture and ktails for s-17..19.

daniel: after weight drop, p99 for s-17..19 came down to ~600ms within 45s, overall p99 now ~0.9s. still above target but improving. stream stalls decreased.

priya: opening a short customer notification draft: "We observed elevated streaming latency impacting a subset of customers in us-west-2 between 14:03-14:25 UTC; a routing configuration issue caused disproportionate load on several shards. Mitigation applied and service restored. Follow-up postmortem to come." ok to send once we confirm final numbers?

maria: yes. gather final impact windows and error rates. Also we need to escalate to eng-runtime: suspected routing policy rollout bug — was config seed applied last night?

alex: there was a routing-policy rollout at 02:10 UTC for prefer-local affinity. I think nodes that joined during scale-up missed the new seed and caused weight skew. I'll tag runtime.

jessica: pinging @eng-runtime

eng-runtime: Investigating. early hypothesis: join-order + async seed apply race. We'll check the seeding controller logs. :mag_right:

maria: current status: p95=220ms, p99=480ms (below SLO). repeating monitoring for 30m. keeping this thread open for handoff if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4123456789 status -> mitigated. Oncall handoff ready in 20m unless escalated. Runbook: create postmortem ticket and assign to eng-runtime, label routing-policy-rollout.

daniel: creating postmortem ticket: PMT-4123, linking metrics snapshots and command history.

priya: I'll send CS note now and prep customer follow-up for the affected accounts. draft included in the ticket.

alex: thanks all. quick action items: (1) eng-runtime to root cause and patch seeding controller (2) infra to add a guard in rollout for nodes with missing seed (3) SRE to add alert for shard-weight-skew > 2x baseline. I'll update the incident doc.

maria: handing off to morning oncall. handing off notes in the incident doc + links. leaving oncall bridge open for 30m.

jessica: :thumbsup: good job team. closing ticket after 1h if stable.
